claims.text: Following up is the hard part, not the work: keeping the context for every person in every conversation, each with a different environment and history.
claims.quote: Following up is the hard part.

claims.text: Every message has a graph of actions, questions, statements, decisions and concepts, with altitudes from the block to the message, the conversation, the company and the contact.
claims.quote: Every message has a graph, and the graph has altitudes

claims.text: Email is a medium: the design brief for a message is the recipient's moment when they open it, not the sender's thread.
claims.quote: The design brief for a message is the recipient's moment when they open it, not the sender's thread.

claims.text: A custom interface per message, thread, topic or question is not an exception; it is how interfaces get made now, moving from genesis through custom to product and commodity.
claims.quote: a custom interface per message, per thread, per topic, per question is not an exception. It is how interfaces get made.

claims.text: In the six agents on one inbox what broke first was not a permission but the follow-up, because the reader agent had to reply when the message was from the owner.
claims.quote: what broke first was not a permission but the follow-up

claims.text: As the story vault treats an article as one projection of a graph, a message to a person is a projection of the conversation graph for one reader at one moment.
claims.quote: A message to a person is the same thing: a projection of the conversation graph, for one reader, at the moment they open it.

claims.text: A reader opening a cold email has about a minute, which is enough for one picture, one link and one easy ask.
claims.quote: a reader opening a cold email has about a minute

claims.text: There is not one UX but many, one per moment, each a mix of agentic, deterministic, informational and thinking threads, mapped from the user down to the components.
claims.quote: So there is not one UX. There are many, one per moment

claims.text: This is what human-in-the-loop looks like when it works: the human is made faster because the surface matches their focus, and every decision is one tap that writes a record.
claims.quote: The human is not a bottleneck approving everything; the human is made faster

claims.text: The measurable test of the title: every question asked of an agent in chat that a page could have shown is the next interface, and asking it twice builds the card.
claims.quote: Ask the same question twice and an agent builds the card.

claims.text: The owner asked for a page listing the PDFs still owed with a place to drop them through a vault's append lane, and an agent built it in an afternoon.
claims.quote: So I asked for an interface, and an agent built one in an afternoon.

claims.text: In eight days from 25 September to 2 October 2026 the agents and the owner went from an empty vault to a working outreach method, including sixteen releases of the CRM's interface.
claims.quote: several versions of the CRM's interface, sixteen releases in all

claims.text: The eight days produced around 230 commits and more than 550 messages between agents, all in files and all versioned.
claims.quote: Around 230 commits and more than 550 messages between agents, all in files, all versioned.

claims.text: Four vault keys were rotated in a single day after an agent's own leak check caught an exposed key.
claims.quote: a rotation of four vault keys in a single day after an agent's own leak check caught an exposed key

value.unit: vault keys rotated in one day

claims.text: Every interface built makes the next one better, because the page is a file in a vault and the next job starts from it.
claims.quote: Every interface you build makes the next one better.

claims.text: Automation creates more work than any inbox can hold, so the interface stops being a convenience and becomes the prioritisation.
claims.quote: Automation creates more work than any inbox can hold.

claims.text: The transport, SMTP or an append lane, stays; above it the graph is the medium and email, cards, voice and boards are views of it.
claims.quote: The graph is the medium. Email, cards, voice and boards are views of it.

claims.text: Earlier futures of email, Wave, AMP for Email, Slack and Hey, died because the inbox is the lowest common denominator everybody already has and they needed the recipient to install something.
claims.quote: the inbox outlived every one of them, because the inbox is the lowest common denominator everybody already has

claims.text: Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook now summarise and reshape mail at the receiving end, and reshape badly because the message gives them nothing to work with.
claims.quote: Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook now summarise and reshape mail at the receiving end, whether the sender wanted it or not.

claims.text: The future of email is sender-served structure, read by the recipient's agent, with the inbox as one view of the graph, and a plain email still works on day one.
claims.quote: The future of email is sender-served structure, read by the recipient's agent, with the inbox as one view of the graph.

claims.text: It can fail in two ways: if recipients' agents never learn to read sender-served structure, or if senders never bother to send it.
claims.quote: It can fail in two ways.

claims.text: Behind the interfaces are ten agents with scoped roles and one human who decides, as of 2 October 2026, each writing only its own folders and talking in files.
claims.quote: Ten agents and one human, each with a scoped role, as of 2 October 2026.

claims.text: Six of the ten agents already have a written Agent Behaviour Policy, including the WhatsApp agent, whose policy was written before any action was switched on.
claims.quote: six of them already have a written Agent Behaviour Policy

claims.text: A page that drops files into a vault, answers questions or lets a model read the CRM is an agent surface with a grant, a mandate, a delta and barriers, so it gets a policy.
claims.quote: A page that drops files into a vault, answers questions on my behalf, or lets a model read my CRM is an agent surface.

claims.text: Every custom interface runs against a vault, uses a read key or a lane token and never a vault key, and calls a model through a bridge that holds no key.
claims.quote: It uses a read key or a lane token, never a vault key

claims.text: Different people's environments, Gmail or Claude or Lovable, produce different policies; the point is that the policy is written and the customising agent knows what it must not loosen.
claims.quote: Different people's environments, Gmail or Claude or Lovable, produce different policies, and that is fine

claims.text: The counts come from the vaults' commit history, and no contact is named and no message is quoted.
claims.quote: Counts come from the vaults' commit history; no contact is named and no message is quoted.

claims.text: The article was revised on 2 October after a review by the RiskMandate agent team, which pointed out that the earlier draft described one page and one afternoon when it was one item in an eight-day stream.
claims.quote: the earlier draft described one page and one afternoon when the page was one item in an eight-day stream

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 1 October 2026, recorded after a week in which an agent built a drag-and-drop page for a set of PDFs the owner owed somebody.
claims.quote: A voice memo on 1 October 2026, recorded after a week in which an agent built a drag-and-drop page

claims.text: The Kit Bag plan put the thesis in a sentence for software generally: the open-source app is the starting point, an agent customises it per person, and the vault is the distribution channel.
claims.quote: the open-source app is the starting point, an agent customises it per person, and the vault is the distribution channel

claims.text: Most of this exists today in pieces; the inbox that joins them is being built now, one custom interface at a time.
claims.quote: The inbox that joins them is being built now, out of those pieces

claims.text: The interfaces are mapped the Wardley way, from the user down to the components, with the strategy maps vault as the method's home.
claims.quote: Mapped the Wardley way, the map starts at the user and works down to the components, not the other way round.
